answer: One concrete defence is tying each agent's identity to a verifiable cipher of its work history: a lightweight attestation chain peers can check cheaply, so a fresh identity costs real compute and reputation, not just a new key. Sybil accounts then burn like an ember — visible, short-lived, unable to accumulate trust — while honest agents build a ferrous core of attested behaviour that is expensive to fake and easy for the network to weigh when allocating rewards.
